query: How can support teams reduce ticket resolution time?

per_column.name: issue_category
per_column.rationale: A clean categorical axis that lets the analyst group resolution_minutes by issue type to find slow categories -- directly useful for reducing resolution time. Category assignments in samples (billing_payment, authentication_access, performance_outage, feature_request, data_quality) are all sound readings of the source text.

per_column.name: requires_external_action
per_column.rationale: External blockers are a strong lever for resolution time analysis, giving a meaningful grouping axis. Grounding is mostly sound (feature_request->not_present, outage->infrastructure), but CS-0001 labeled 'awaiting_customer_info' when the customer supplied full details and awaits a corrected invoice, and CS-0002 labeled 'awaiting_engineering_fix' where the text points to the customer's IT SSO push, showing some unwarranted inference.

per_column.name: external_dependency_type
per_column.rationale: Identifies specific external dependencies, a useful complement for pinpointing where delays originate. However CS-0001 asserts 'payment_processor' when the text only mentions a duplicate line item and ACH payment (not a processor issue), and CS-0002 asserts 'identity_provider' where SSO is only suspected -- both confident specifics the text does not clearly support.

per_column.name: resolution_action
per_column.rationale: The action/disposition taken is highly relevant for identifying efficient resolution paths and where investigation time is spent. Most sample values are reasonable, but resolution_action is a produced label not stated in the source (the tickets describe requests, not outcomes), so values like 'billing_credit_refund' for CS-0001 are plausible inferences rather than grounded facts, introducing some speculation.

judge.rationale: All four added columns give genuine, non-redundant analytical axes (issue type, external blocking, dependency, resolution path) that a support team could group resolution_minutes on to find drivers of slow resolution -- strongly aligned with the query. Categorical columns are well grounded, but the two dependency-oriented columns and resolution_action occasionally assert confident specifics (payment_processor, identity_provider, particular resolution outcomes) that the source text only weakly implies, lowering overall groundedness while usefulness remains high.
